title: Removal of normal-flat chart relations modulo a finite jet without reducedness
statement:
Let $(T,\mathfrak M,k)$ be a nonzero commutative regular local ring, with residue field $k=T/\mathfrak M$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-residue-field]. Fix a regular system of parameters $(x_0,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_s)$, where $r,s\geq0$, and put $P=(x_0,\ldots,x_r)$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Let $\mathfrak a\subseteq P$ be an ideal, put $R=T/\mathfrak a$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak M/\mathfrak a$, $I=P/\mathfrak a$, $A=T/P=R/I$, and assume $G=\operatorname{gr}_I R$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Set $S=G\otimes_A k$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and $B=k[X_0,\ldots,X_r]$, with all variables of degree one [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-pc-standard-graded-algebra].
Assume no minimal prime of $R$ contains $I$, where a minimal prime contains no strictly smaller prime. Let $z\in\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}R)$ be over $\mathfrak m$ and belong to the chart $\operatorname{Spec}R[I/\bar x_0]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-nagata-affine-blowup, def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. Put
$$D_T=T[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(x_0t_i-x_i:1\leq i\leq r),\qquad T'=(D_T)_{\mathfrak p'},$$ [def-trf-permissible-coordinate-chart-ring]
where $\mathfrak p'$ is the inverse image of $z$ under the surjection $D_T\twoheadrightarrow R[I/\bar x_0]$, $t_i\mapsto\bar x_i/\bar x_0$. Assume $T'$ is regular local, let $R_z=\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}R),z}$, and put $\mathfrak a'=\ker(T'\twoheadrightarrow R_z)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].
Let $\mathfrak M'$ be the maximal ideal of $T'$, let $H=(x_0,y_1,\ldots,y_s)T'$, and let $\mathfrak p\subset k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$ be the prime obtained from $\mathfrak p'$ modulo $\mathfrak M D_T$. Put $L=k[t]_{\mathfrak p}$ and $N=\mathfrak pL$. The quotient $T'/H$ is identified with $L$ via the displayed chart presentation. For a local ring with maximal ideal $K$, define the order of $h$ to be $\sup\{n:h\in K^n\}$ and its finite-order initial form to be $h\bmod K^{n+1}\in K^n/K^{n+1}$ [def-trf-local-standard-basis-invariants].
Let $m\geq1$ and let $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in\mathfrak a$ have finite orders $1\leq d_1\leq\cdots\leq d_m$ and belong to $P^{d_i}$. Suppose their initial forms $\phi_i\in k[X]_{d_i}$ minimally generate $\ker(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M}T\to\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}R)$ in $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M}T=k[X,Y]$ [def-trf-adic-initial-ideal-generator-degrees]. Put $g_i=f_i/x_0^{d_i}\in T'$ using the ambient chart embedding into $T[1/x_0]$. Fix $0\leq b<m$ and an integer $d\geq1$ with $d_j\leq d$ for $j\leq b$ and $d_i\geq d$ for $i>b$. For each $j\leq b$ suppose
$$\phi_j(1,t)/1\in N^{d_j},\qquad q_j=g_j-w_j,\qquad w_j\in H(g_1,\ldots,g_{j-1})T',\qquad\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak M'}q_j=d_j.$$
Put $J=(q_1,\ldots,q_b)T'$ and assume the finite-jet generation condition $\mathfrak a'\subseteq J+\mathfrak M'^{\,d}$. Then
$$J\cap(H+\mathfrak M'^{\,d})\subseteq HJ+\mathfrak M'^{\,d}.$$
All intersections and sums here are of ideals of $T'$. The ideal generated by an empty family is zero. No reducedness hypothesis is imposed on $R$.

source.place: Hironaka (1970), basic assumptions (2.1)-(2.2), pp.155-156, and Lemma 20, (20.3)-(20.12), pp.177-181: finite-jet ideal-intersection formulation of coefficient elimination. Read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival original WANTED. No Stacks tag states this specialized lemma.

proof.text: Write $\theta_i=\phi_i(1,t)/1$. For $v\in P^h$, expand $v=\sum_{|\alpha|=h}a_\alpha x^\alpha$. Its divided image is $v/x_0^h=\sum a_\alpha t^{(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r)}$ in the ambient chart. Reducing modulo $H$ reduces the coefficients modulo $\mathfrak M$, giving the dehomogenized degree-$h$ initial class. Thus $g_i\bmod H=\theta_i$. By [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], the target chart is a subring of $R[1/\bar x_0]$. Multiplication by $\bar x_0$ is injective on this subring and its localization: if $\bar x_0(c/s)=0$, some localization denominator annihilates $\bar x_0c$, hence also $c$. For $v\in\mathfrak a\cap P^h$, the image of its divided expression is killed by $\bar x_0^h$, hence is zero. Therefore $v/x_0^h\in\mathfrak a'$, and every $g_i\in\mathfrak a'$. The triangular identities give $(q_1,\ldots,q_j)=(g_1,\ldots,g_j)$ successively: $w_j$ lies in the preceding ideal in either family. In particular $J\subseteq\mathfrak a'$, $w_j\in HJ$ and $q_j\bmod H=\theta_j$. The given local quotient $T'/H=L$ gives $\mathfrak M'/H=N$, so $N^v$ is the image of $\mathfrak M'^v$ for every $v\geq0$.

source.place: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), (19.1)–(19.2), p.176, and the beginning of the proof of Lemma 20, p.177; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf. Archival original WANTED. Online source read by Q47; finite-jet assembly supplied by the agent. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text:
Take a homogeneous syzygy $\sum_{j\leq b}C_j\phi_j=0$ of total degree $h\geq1$, with $C_j=0$ when $d_j>h$. Lift each polynomial coefficient to $T$ and substitute $x$ to get $c_j\in P^{h-d_j}$. Then $u=\sum c_jf_j\in\mathfrak a\cap P^h$ has zero degree-$h$ initial class, so $u\in\mathfrak M^{h+1}$. Apply [lem-trf-normal-flat-initial-coefficient-lifting] with $n=h$: its regular-local, parameter, normal-flat and minimal-initial-generator hypotheses are exactly ours, and it requires no reducedness. We obtain $p_i\in\mathfrak M P^{h-d_i}$ for $d_i\leq h$, with $v=u-\sum p_if_i\in\mathfrak a\cap P^{h+1}$. Expand each $p_i$ in degree-$(h-d_i)$ parameter monomials with coefficients in $\mathfrak M$. Since $\mathfrak M T'=(x_0,y)T'=H$, its divided image $p_i/x_0^{h-d_i}$ lies in $H$. Step 1 gives $v/x_0^{h+1}\in\mathfrak a'$. The identity obtained by dividing by $x_0^h$ is therefore
$$\sum_{j\leq b}(c_j/x_0^{h-d_j})g_j=\sum_{d_i\leq h}(p_i/x_0^{h-d_i})g_i+x_0(v/x_0^{h+1})\in H\mathfrak a'.$$
These are identities of the divided polynomial expressions in the given ambient chart, hence in $T'$.

source.place: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), (20.4)–(20.7), pp.178–179; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf. Archival original WANTED. Online source read by Q47; finite-jet assembly supplied by the agent. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text:
Put $E=HJ+\mathfrak M'^d$. For $z\in J\cap(H+\mathfrak M'^d)$ choose $z=\sum_{j\leq b}h_jq_j$ and set $\beta_j=h_j\bmod H$. Induct on $e=1,\ldots,d$, keeping a sum $s=\sum h_jq_j$ such that $s-z\in E$, $s\in H+\mathfrak M'^d$, and $\beta_j\in N^{\max(e-d_j,0)}$. The initial coefficients satisfy these conditions at $e=1$. Suppose $e<d$. Modulo $H$ the sum $\sum\beta_j\theta_j$ belongs to $N^d\subseteq N^{e+1}$. Terms with $d_j>e$ separately lie in $N^{e+1}$, since $\theta_j\in N^{d_j}$. Apply [lem-trf-projective-order-leading-syzygies] to the active indices $j\leq b$ with $d_j\leq e$, using its integer $e$. Their forms are nonzero homogeneous of degree $d_j$ and belong to $U_{d_j}$ by hypothesis; their coefficients belong to $N^{e-d_j}$. It supplies finitely many homogeneous syzygies $(C_{vj})$ of degrees $1\leq h_v\leq e$ and $a_v\in N^{e-h_v}$, satisfying
$$\beta_j-\sum_v a_v\delta(C_{vj})\in N^{e-d_j+1}$$
on the active indices. Extend each syzygy by zero on inactive indices, so it is a syzygy of the whole prefix. Here $\delta(C)=C(1,t)/1$.

source.place: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), (20.3)–(20.4), pp.177–178, using Lemma 17, pp.172–173; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf. Archival original WANTED. Online source read by Q47; finite-jet assembly supplied by the agent. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text:
For every syzygy just obtained choose the polynomial lifts $c_{vj}$ from Step 2, and lift each $a_v$ to $A_v\in T'$. Put $k_j=\sum_v A_vc_{vj}/x_0^{h_v-d_j}$, omitting zero terms when $d_j>h_v$. The divided expressions have residues $\delta(C_{vj})$, so $k_j\bmod H=\sum_v a_v\delta(C_{vj})$. Step 2 shows $\sum_j(c_{vj}/x_0^{h_v-d_j})g_j\in H\mathfrak a'$. Subtracting the corresponding combination of $w_j\in HJ$ gives the same assertion with $q_j$ in place of $g_j$. Summing with coefficients $A_v$ gives $\sum_jk_jq_j\in H\mathfrak a'$. The assumed finite-jet generation implies
$$H\mathfrak a'\subseteq HJ+H\mathfrak M'^d\subseteq HJ+\mathfrak M'^{d+1}\subseteq E.$$
Replace $h_j$ by $h_j-k_j$. The new represented sum is congruent to the old one modulo $E$, and still lies in $H+\mathfrak M'^d$ because $E\subseteq H+\mathfrak M'^d$. The congruences from Step 3 give the required $N^{e-d_j+1}$ membership on active indices. For inactive indices $k_j=0$ and $d_j\geq e+1$, so their next bound remains $N^0=L$. This proves the induction step.

source.place: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), (20.5)–(20.12), pp.179–181; finite-coefficient version of the same elimination; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf. Archival original WANTED. Online source read by Q47; finite-jet assembly supplied by the agent. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: At $e=d$, choose $h_j^0\in\mathfrak M'^{\max(d-d_j,0)}$ lifting the final residue $\beta_j$; Step 1 permits this choice. Then $h_j-h_j^0\in H$ and $h_j^0q_j\in\mathfrak M'^d$, since $q_j\in\mathfrak M'^{d_j}$. Thus the final sum lies in $HJ+\mathfrak M'^d=E$. It is congruent to the original $z$ modulo $E$, proving the desired inclusion. If $b=0$, $J=0$ and the assertion is immediate. If $d=1$, the induction has no transitions and the final argument applies directly. No step used reducedness of $R$: injectivity in Step 1 comes from the chart subring of a localization; the coefficient-lifting statement explicitly allows nonreduced $R$; the syzygy statement is over an arbitrary field.
